title: Making Friends
passages: Making a friend often begins with something small. A smile across a room, a shared joke, or a question asked with real interest can open a door. It takes a little COURAGE to say hello first, because no one knows how the other person will answer. Friendship grows when two people notice what they have in common and also enjoy what makes them different. Listening closely is a quiet kind of GENEROSITY. When someone feels truly heard, they begin to feel safe, and trust starts to take root like a seed in warm soil.

Keeping a friend asks for PATIENCE. Friends sometimes disagree, and saying sorry can feel hard, yet a sincere apology often makes a bond stronger than before. It is lovely to wonder how friendship looks in other places. Perhaps somewhere far away, two friends are sharing a meal, singing together, or walking side by side without needing many words. Every corner of the world may have its own way of showing LOYALTY, and each one is worth being curious about. What stays the same everywhere, maybe, is the warm feeling of being RECOGNIZED and welcomed just as you are.
